clue.text: Fresh support for the American dollar?

parts.note: fresh as in new and unripe means green
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A call for new backing for the US currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as a nickname: US banknotes are printed green on the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenback is the slang name for a US banknote, from its green-printed reverse side.

clue.text: A Spanish wine jar I' smashed when empty?

indicators.note: a jar that is smashed has its pieces scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, with a stray printing mark
something empty holds nothing, and nothing is the round letter O

explanation.surface: A jar of Spanish wine breaks once it has been drunk dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix JAR, I and O (empty, nothing) to give the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the La Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: The salad food that's the last thing I have cut down on

parts.note: the last thing of all is the end

indicators.note: the word have shortened to its contracted form, as in the apostrophe form of I have

parts.note: the verb to possess, here written short

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to cut back on salad leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut down' trims HAVE to VE, as in the contraction I've; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy chicory plant eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Government-plan -for-the economy

explanation.surface: A plain description of a state's financial plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed hyphens are scanning marks; the clue reads 'Government plan for the economy'. The yearly statement of tax and spending is one sense; the cheap, economy class (a budget airline) is the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A government's annual financial statement is the budget, and budget also describes low-cost, economy goods.

clue.text: Smart ' girl that is after a share of the proceeds

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is placed following the share

parts.note: a cut is one's portion of the takings
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A girl is chasing her slice of the profits.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray mark after 'Smart' is a printing blemish; the definition is 'smart girl', an attractive, clever-looking one.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive, pert young woman, which suits a smart, pretty girl.

clue.text: No reply from the editor?

parts.note: a writer submitting work hopes for an acceptance; the note a publisher sends back saying no is the editor's reply that is a refusal

explanation.surface: A writer waits in vain for word from an editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No reply' looks like silence, but the editor does reply, with a refusal: the reply is a no.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor turning down a manuscript sends a printed refusal note with it.

clue.text: A region that isn't devoid of humanity

definitions.text: A region that isn't devoid of humanity

parts.words: A region that isn't devoid of humanity
parts.note: humanity read as people rather than kindness: an area full of inhabitants

explanation.surface: Somewhere that still has some compassion left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humanity' suggests kindness; here it means human beings, so the region simply has people living in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A district with inhabitants, a settled zone rather than a wilderness.

clue.text: Impressive consequence of a sell-out, maybe

definitions.text: Impressive consequence of a sell-out, maybe

parts.words: Impressive consequence of a sell-out, maybe
parts.note: when a book's first print run sells out, the publisher prints it again; 'impressive' puns on a printing impression

explanation.surface: Selling out has impressive results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressive' plays on impression, a print run: a sold-out book gets a fresh printing.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that sells out its first run is reissued in a new printed version.

clue.text: He's not much good as a linesman

definitions.text: He's not much good as a linesman

parts.words: He's not much good as a linesman
parts.note: a linesman here is a writer of lines of verse rather than a football or tennis official

explanation.surface: A poor official running the line at a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' suggests a sports official; it is someone who writes lines of verse, badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is an inferior writer of verse, a poor versifier.

clue.text: In vain he sought to get gold from St Michael

definitions.text: In vain he sought to get gold

indicators.note: the answer is made out of the letters of these words, worked from them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man tried in vain to get gold from a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: St Michael was the brand of the British store Marks & Spencer; its letters rearrange into the gold-seeker.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval practitioners of alchemy tried to turn base metals into gold, never succeeding.

clue.text: Ring an agent back at Covent ' Garden?

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: the article and the agent are read in reverse order of letters

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: Telephoning a representative from Covent Garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Covent Garden is home to London's Royal Opera House, so the place stands for the art; the stray mark is a printing blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Royal Opera House stands in Covent Garden, so the district's name stands for the art staged there.

clue.text: Congruent peer

explanation.surface: Two words that both describe matching.
explanation.definitionFit: Congruent shapes are identical in size, and a peer is one's equivalent in rank.

clue.text: Acute distress on the coast of Morocco

indicators.note: distress as damage to a surface, so the word is roughed up into new order

explanation.surface: Severe hardship somewhere on the North African shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acute distress' reads as severe suffering; 'distress' is the anagram signal working on ACUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceuta is a Spanish enclave on the North African shore facing Gibraltar.

clue.text: Disposal of a crop exported from the South Sea islands

definitions.text: exported from the South Sea islands

indicators.note: disposal as arrangement: the letters are disposed in a new way

explanation.surface: Selling off a harvest shipped from the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposal' suggests getting rid of; it also means arranging, which reorders A CROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra, dried coconut kernel, is a chief product shipped out of the Pacific islands.

clue.text: One who is extremely interested in politics

definitions.text: One who is extremely interested in politics

parts.words: One who is extremely interested in politics
parts.note: extremely read as holding extreme views, not merely very keen

explanation.surface: A person with a great enthusiasm for politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely interested' sounds like very keen; it means holding extreme political opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is an extremist, someone whose political opinions go far beyond the mainstream.

clue.text: A mass rising on India's northern border

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd rises up near India's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'rising' reads the mass upwards. Assam lies in the north-east, along the borders with Bhutan and Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in the north-east of India, bordering Bhutan and Tibet.

clue.text: Indian pony seen at the Edinburgh Festival

explanation.surface: An Indian horse appears at the Scottish arts festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Military Tattoo, a military display, is held during the Edinburgh Festival; the Indian pony is also called a tattoo (tattu).
explanation.definitionFit: Tattoo is an Anglo-Indian name for a native-bred pony, and also the military display held at Edinburgh Castle.

clue.text: Red man I am no longer quiet about

indicators.note: the call for silence goes around the past tense

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
if I am no longer something, I was it

explanation.surface: A Native American speaker says he is no longer silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the call for quiet round the past tense. Siwash is a dated, now offensive term for a Native American of the Pacific north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Siwash was a dated, offensive term for a Native American of the north-west US and Canada.

clue.text: Downtrodden ways

parts.note: downtrodden read literally: routes that feet have trodden down

explanation.surface: Customs of the oppressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downtrodden' suggests oppressed people; read literally it is ground walked flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracks worn by walkers are routes trodden down by feet.

clue.text: A man in the firing line

definitions.text: A man in the firing line

parts.words: A man in the firing line
parts.note: firing read as stoking a furnace, not shooting: the job of feeding coal to a ship's or engine's fire

explanation.surface: A soldier exposed to enemy fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firing line' suggests battle; it is the work of firing a boiler with coal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker tends a furnace, feeding fuel to a steam engine's or ship's fire.

clue.text: Two Poles cutting a tree for a saintly archbishop

indicators.note: the poles cut into the tree name, splitting it

parts.note: an elm is a tree
the north and south poles are N and S

explanation.surface: Two Polish men fell a tree for a holy churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland; they are the compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: St Anselm was an Archbishop of Canterbury in the 11th century, later canonised.

clue.text: Device that is, set to arouse fear

definitions.text: Device that is, set to arouse

explanation.surface: A gadget designed to frighten people.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'is' is misplaced in print; the two definitions are a device set to rouse someone (a clock's bell) and fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell set to wake a sleeper and a feeling of sudden fright share one word.

clue.text: An arcade made with timber I located in Georgia?

parts.note: a log is a length of timber

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Wooden arcade construction in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Located in' puts I inside GA; 'made with' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A loggia is a gallery with open arches on one side, a kind of arcade.

clue.text: Article torn out by a girl from Italy

indicators.note: out as in disordered, so the letters are put out of place

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
rent means torn
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news story ripped up by an Italian girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' mixes A and RENT into RENAT; 'by' joins the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Renata is an Italian female forename.

clue.text: An unfinished picture frame?

parts.note: the frame holds a picture that is still being painted, a stand for work in progress

explanation.surface: A frame for a picture that is not yet done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture frame' suggests a border round a finished painting; this frame supports one still being painted.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's stand holds a canvas while it is still being painted.

clue.text: French law about French currency

parts.note: loi is French for law
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A French statute concerning money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Currency' is read as something with a current: a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is France's longest river, and a river is a thing with a current.

clue.text: Seafood strike, in the Civil Service

indicators.note: the strike word sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CS is the abbreviation for Civil Service
to lam is to hit or thrash

explanation.surface: A strike over shellfish breaks out among civil servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like industrial action; it is LAM, to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clams are edible shellfish, eaten as seafood.

clue.text: A capital atmosphere in a small business establishment

indicators.note: the atmosphere word sits within the company abbreviation

parts.note: Co is the short form of company, a business
air is atmosphere

explanation.surface: Fine ambience in a little firm's premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' tells the solver to shorten company to CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt.

clue.text: Sea-parrot fluttering in a creamery?.

definitions.note: describes where the machine is found rather than naming it

indicators.note: a bird fluttering is in restless motion, so its letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A puffin flaps about inside a dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea-parrot is a puffin; the definition is by location, the machine that splits cream from milk in a dairy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream separator is a dairy centrifuge that splits cream from milk.
